### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace (200 of 200) contained A02, A04, A05 and A06 exactly once, and the only observed successor chain was A02 → A04 → A05 → A06: A02's observed outgoing transitions went entirely to A04, A04's entirely to A05, and no outgoing transition was observed from A06, which sat at the end of the trace. A01 and A03 appeared in 0 of 200 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, POS003, POS005]
- In the later window, every trace (200 of 200) contained A02, A03, A05, A06 and A01 exactly once, and the observed successor chain is A02 → A03 → A05 → A06 → A01: A02 now leads entirely to A03, A03 leads entirely to A05, and A06 is now always followed by A01, which closes the trace at the last position. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, POS001, POS002, POS005, REL005]
- The participation swap is complete: A04 fell from 200 of 200 traces to 0 of 200, while A03 and A01 rose from 0 of 200 to 200 of 200; no activity repeats within a trace in either window (each present activity occurs once per trace). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- Positions match a like-for-like substitution plus an appended step: A04 previously sat at about one third of the trace; A03 now sits at about one quarter and A01 at the very end. A05 and A06 keep their relative order (A05 at about 0.5 before A06 at about 0.75 in the later window); their normalized positions shifted (A05 from about 0.67 to 0.50, A06 from 1.00 to 0.75) simply because traces grew from four to five events. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Pairwise relations agree throughout: A01 moved from never co-occurring with A02, A03, A05 or A06 to co-occurring with all of them, always after them; A02–A03 moved from "A02 only" to always together with A02 first; the pairs A02–A04, A03–A04, A04–A05 and A04–A06 moved from always together (A04 after A02, before A05/A06) to one-sided because A04 disappeared. [REL001, REL002, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the linear main flow was restructured in the later window: A04, which previously always ran between A02 and A05, is no longer executed; A03 now runs in that position (A02 → A03 → A05); and A01 was added as a new closing step after A06 — in short, the observed chain changed from A02 → A04 → A05 → A06 to A02 → A03 → A05 → A06 → A01. The signs are direct and mutually consistent: participation is all-or-nothing (0 of 200 vs 200 of 200) for A04, A03 and A01; the successor changes sit exactly at the splice points; every pairwise relation matches a single deterministic sequence per window; and all 24 qualifying control-flow items compare with about 0.12 expected by chance, so the pattern as a whole is far beyond what random re-splits of an unchanged process produce. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, REL006, REL009, screening]

Limitations: the evidence shows the two window snapshots but cannot tell whether A04's removal, A03's insertion and A01's addition were one substitution or independent changes, nor whether the new flow appeared abruptly at the boundary or the windows simply fall on either side of a gradual transition. An important competing explanation that cannot be ruled out is a shift in the case mix between the windows (each sample drawing from a different existing variant) rather than a modification of one flow; the all-or-nothing participation makes plain sampling noise implausible, but nothing here shows what happened between the two windows. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, screening]

Other differences: none beyond the consequences of the main hypothesis — the small normalized position shifts of A05 and A06 follow from traces growing from four to five events, not from a relocation of these steps. [POS004, POS005]
